description: Verified former stations/halts on the Bala and Festiniog Railway between Blaenau Ffestiniog and Trawsfynydd, in order south-bound. Coordinates from Wikipedia infoboxes (English Heritage/National Grid references); route_index/distance_km_from_blaenau computed by snapping each station to the nearest point on the OSM-derived trackbed polyline.

stations.name: Blaenau Ffestiniog
stations.closed_to_passengers: 1960 (original GWR station); line to Trawsfynydd mothballed 1998
stations.status_2026: Still an active station today — southern terminus of the Conwy Valley Line (Transport for Wales) and northern terminus of the heritage narrow-gauge Ffestiniog Railway to Porthmadog. The route concept would start from this live station, not a dead site.

stations.name: Festiniog (Llan Ffestiniog)
stations.closed_to_passengers: 4 January 1960; line closed completely 27/28 January 1961; briefly reopened for a 1989 tourist special
stations.status_2026: Site demolished by 2011; mothballed trackbed runs through the former station site, overgrown. Subject of a 2016-2020 community clearance effort that did not result in reopening.

stations.name: Maentwrog Road
stations.closed_to_passengers: 4 January 1960; freight continued about a year longer
stations.status_2026: Station building and stationmaster's house are long-standing private residences. The A470 road bridge immediately north was rebuilt in 2002 in a way that preserved the rail line beneath/beside it.

stations.name: Trawsfynydd Lake Halt
stations.closed_to_passengers: 4 January 1960; reopened from the north 1964 for power-station traffic but the halt itself was never reused for passengers; line mothballed 17 October 1998
stations.status_2026: Platform remains, rediscovered under vegetation by 2017 volunteer clearance; no services since 1960.

stations.name: Trawsfynydd
stations.closed_to_passengers: 4 January 1960; closed completely 28 January 1961; road transport carried residual freight until 4 May 1964
stations.status_2026: Former station building is a private residence; former goods yard/military-camp sidings now in agricultural use. The 1999-era engine shed was last reported standing (used as a store).
